HELD: The scope of entry 24(e) of notification no. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and 54(e) of notification no. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 are limited to services in relation to agriculture produce and cultivation of plants. [Para 25]

As per the scheme of classification of services appended to Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and its corresponding State tax Notification No. 46/ST-2, dated 30-6-2017 the service code 997212 is for renting or leasing services involving own or leased non-residential property. Such services attract 18 per cent GST as per Sr. No. 16 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and its corresponding State tax Notification No. 46/ST-2, dated 30-6-2017. [Para 26]

Since, as per the copy of contract/agreement with Hafed, the applicant is providing both the services, i.e., the support services in relation to agricultural produce as well as Real Estate Services in terms of SAC 997212, and since both these services are capable of being provided independent of each other, these cannot be understood to be naturally bundled and supplied conjointly in the ordinary course of business. Therefore, the applicant has/is providing 'Mixed Supply' as per section 2(74) of the CGST/HGST Act, 2017 and attract tax rate of that particular supply which attracts the highest rate of tax in terms of section 8(b). [Para 27]

Thus, the services, i.e., leasing of immovable property and support services in relation to agricultural produce, provided by the applicant are in the nature of 'Mixed Supply' in terms of section 2(74) and hence, attract 9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent HGST (18 per cent IGST) as applicable to SAC 997212. [Para 27]

Lease of plots to PMC for PMC's Commissioner's and Mayor's residences The applicant has mainly stated that the said residences are the places from where the PMC Commissioner as well as the Mayor function. This submission cannot be accepted. The Commissioner operates from his own office and so does the Mayor. The very fact that the applicant has submitted that the plots are for residences would mean that the same are for the personal use of the concerned officials. Construction of residence for officials cannot be considered to be a function envisaged under article 243W of the Constitution of India. The Authority does not agree with the applicant's contention that the leasing of land for construction of building for use as PMC Commissioner's and PMC Mayor's residences falls within the scope of Entry No. 2 of the Twelfth Schedule to the Constitution of India relating to 'Regulation of land-use and construction of buildings' or within the scope of any of the Entries of the Twelfth Schedule to the Constitution of India. Clause (vi) Sr. No. 3 of the Notification 11/2017 -Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-04-2017 reads as:

Composite supply of works contract as defined in clause 119 of section 2 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 provided to the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority or a governmental authority by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of -

(c) a residential complex predominantly meant for self-use or the use of their employees or other persons specified in paragraph 3 of the Schedule III of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017

The 'other persons' mentioned in the above clause (vi) are Members of Parliament, State Legislatures, Panchayats, Municipalities and other local authorities; persons who hold any post in pursuance of the provisions of the Constitution in that capacity; and Chairperson or Member or a Director in a body established by the Central Government or a State Government of local authority……..

From the above it is seen that even construction of residential complex predominantly meant for self use or use of the employees of Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority or a governmental authority is liable to GST.

In view of Sr. No. 3, clause (vi) (c) and Sr. No. 16 of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, lease of plots for such constructions to be carried out, as in the instant case, will not be exempt and will be covered under Heading No. 9972. [Para 5]

Ltd.) is 100 per cent Madhya Pradesh State Government hold company - State Government of Madhya Pradesh awarded a contract to applicant to construct a Thermal Power Project - Further applicant awarded a contract to one 'S' towards construction of certain residential quarters at Thermal Power Project - Whether work contract awarded by applicant to 'S' for construction of residential quarters at Thermal Power Project shall attract GST at rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) under Heading No. 9954 - Held, yes [Para 8.1][In favour of revenue]GST: Where State Government of Madhya Pradesh awarded a contract to applicant, a 100 per cent State Government hold company, to construct a Thermal Power Project and further applicant awarded a contract to one 'S' towards construction of certain residential quarters at Thermal Power Project, work contract awarded by applicant to 'S' for construction of residential quarters shall attract GST at rate of 18 per cent under Heading No. 9954

FACT: The applicant (M.P. Power Generating Co. Ltd.) is 100 per cent Madhya Pradesh State Government hold company.

The State Government of Madhya Pradesh awarded a contract to the applicant to construct a Thermal Power Project.

Further the applicant has awarded a contract to one Shreeji Infrastructure India (P.) Ltd. towards construction of certain residential quarters at aforesaid Thermal Power Project.

It sought advance ruling on the following questions:

-

Rate of GST on contract for construction of building and structure for colony at Thermal Power Project as per Notification No. 11/2017 as amended by Notification No. 24/2017 and further amended vide Notification No. 31/2017.

-

Rate of GST on construction contract of residential quarters at various power houses of the applicant as per Notification No. 11/2017 as amended by Notification No. 24/2017 and further amended vide Notification No. 31/2017.

The applicant submitted before the Authority for Advance Ruling that Shreeji Infrastructure India (P.) Ltd. has obtained an advance ruling on the issue raised in the instant application vide order No. 15/2018, dated 18-10-2018, but this fact was not brought to the notice of the Authority that the work is being entrusted to the applicant by Government of Madhya Pradesh and hence the applicant is filing a fresh advance ruling application.

HELD: The issue raised in the instant application has been duly decided by the Authority in the matter of application filed by Shreeji Infrastructure India (P.) Ltd., Inre [2018] 98 taxmann.com 438/[2019] 71 GST 40 (AAR-MP). The Authority vide order dated 18-10-2018 had ruled that the works contract service of construction of residential quarters allotted to the applicant (Shreeji Infrastructure (P.) Ltd.) by M.P. Power Generating Co. Ltd. will merit classification under Heading No. 9954 and would attract GST at the rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST). [Para 7.3]

In the instant application, the applicant has sought a fresh ruling on the same contract awarded to Shreeji Infrastructure (P.) Ltd. arguing that the aforesaid order dated 18-10-2018 is not applicable as the information before the Authority was insufficient and inconclusive to arrive at the ruling. [Para 7.4]

The applicant has argued that the Government of Madhya Pradesh incorporated M.P. Power Generating Co. Ltd. with an object to construct, operate and maintain electricity system as defined in section 2(25) of Electricity Act, 2003 (Power Projects). It has been argued by the applicant that the work of power project includes the entrusting all work related to that project including the work of construction of residential colonies as they are in relation to the power project which is entrusted by the Government. [Para 7.5]

The Authority is not inclined to subscribe to the contentions of the applicant. The fact still remains that the sole work entrusted by the Government of Madhya Pradesh to the applicant is of generation of electricity (power) in the State of Madhya Pradesh. Construction of residential quarters though within the precincts of power plant cannot by any stretch of argument and imagination be termed as the work entrusted to applicant. [Para 7.6]

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Kerala State Goods And Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction of road, bridges and other infrastructure - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services)- Section 2(119), of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant is engaged in providing services of construction including materials and labour as per tender requirements - They have received a work order from Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre for construction of a building for space transportation system - It is a composite contract which includes supply of materials as well as service - They have also received another work order from Infrastructure Kerala Ltd., a Public Private Partnership Company promoted by Government of Kerala, for development of Medical College which includes construction of road, bridges and other infrastructure - Applicant has requested for advance ruling on rate of tax applicable for above works contracts awarded by Government authorities - Whether since services provided by applicant under both contracts fall under definition of works contract under section 2(119) and services are being provided to Central Government and State Government, applicant is eligible for concessional rate of GST of 12 per cent prescribed in Sl. No. 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 as amended - Held, yes [Para 9]GST: Where services of construction with material provided by applicant under construction contracts awarded by Government authorities fall under definition of works contract under section 2(119) and services being provided to Central and State government, applicant will be eligible for concessional rate of GST of 12 per cent prescribed in Sl. No. 3 (vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017, dated 28-6-2017

FACT: The applicant is carrying on business in the housing and construction sector. They are engaged in providing services of construction including materials and labour as per the tender requirements. They have received a work order from Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre for the construction of a building for space transportation system. It is a composite contract which includes supply of materials as well as service. They have also received another work order from a Public Private Partnership Company promoted by Government of Kerala, for the development of Medical College, Thiruvananthapuram which includes construction of road, bridges and other infrastructure.

The applicant has requested for advance ruling on the rate of tax applicable for the above works contracts awarded by the Government authorities.

HELD: As per section 2(119), 'works contract' means a contract for building, construction, fabrication, completion, erection, installation, fitting out, improvement, modification, repair, maintenance, renovation, alteration or commissioning of any immovable property wherein transfer of property in goods (whether as goods or in some other form) is involved in the execution of such contract.[Para 5]

On a perusal of the work orders and the agreements entered by the applicant it is clear that the services rendered by the applicant clearly falls within the definition of works contract under section 2(119).[Para 6]

Since the services provided by the applicant under both the contracts fall under the definition of works contract under section 2(119) and the services being provided to the Central Government and State Government, the applicant is eligible for the concessional rate of GST of 12 per cent prescribed in Sl. No. 3(vi)(a) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 as amended.

In view of the observations stated above, it is ruled that the services provided by the applicant under both the contracts being composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 provided to the Central Government and State Government by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry or any other business or profession is covered under entry at Sl. No. 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 as amended and attract GST at the rate of 12 per cent [6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent SGST].

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 - Applicant has entered into a contract for construction of a medical college with HITES which is a Government of India enterprise - Applicant has submitted that it was a sub-contractor to main contractor HITES as it is an executive agency of Central Government - Accordingly, it sought an advance ruling on question as to whether service of work contract provided by applicant as sub-contractor is taxable at rate of 12 percent for period prior to 25-1-2018 when Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 was amended by Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 - Whether GST rate of 12 per cent prescribed under Serial No. (ix) of Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 is effective prospectively from 25-1-2018 - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, service of work contract provided by applicant as sub-contractor is not taxable at rate of 12 per cent for period before 25-1-2018 i.e. prior to issuance of amended Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate) dated 25-1-2018 - Held, yes [Paras 25 and 26]GST : Service of work contract for construction of a medical college provided by applicant as sub-contractor to a Government enterprise is not taxable at rate of 12 per cent for period before 25-1-2018 i.e., prior to issuance of amended Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate) dated 25-1-2018

FACT: HITES which is a Government of India enterprise and executive agency of Ministry of Health & Welfare, Government of India, floated a tender for the construction of a medical college. Accordingly, the applicant has entered into a contract for construction of a medical college with HITES. The applicant submitted that scope of work included construction of multi storied building including water supply, sanitary and plumbing comprehensive firefighting/protection system, internal & external electrification, HVAC works, Lifts, WTP, STP, ETP, CCTV and security system, solar panel, PA system, EPABX/communication system, LAN system, site development works such as internal road & site levelling, sewer and storm water drainage work etc.

The applicant has sought an advance ruling on question as to whether the service of work contract provided by the applicant as sub-contractor is taxable at rate of 12 per cent for period prior to 25-1-2018 when Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 was amended by Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate), dated 25-1-2018.

HELD: The applicant in the present case is a sub-contractor providing services to main contractor i.e. HITES, who is an executing agency of the Ministry of Health & Welfare, Govt. of India. The work of construction of medical college has been entrusted to HITES by the Central Govt. and the applicant has provided services in the capacity of a sub-contractor. [Para 16]

To examine whether the applicant is eligible for GST at the rate of 12 per cent prior to the 25-1-2018, the main Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 vide which Central Government notified rates applicable on the services has to be referred. [Para 18]

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction services - Heading No.9954 (Construction services) - Construction service is provided by applicant contractor under project 'La-Riveria' - Apartment in said project is less than 60 sq. mt. carpet area - Whether said project is an affordable housing project which qualifies for application of lower rate of CGST of 6 per cent and SGST at rate of 6 per cent w.e.f. 25-1-2018 as provided in Sl. No. 3 of Notification No.11/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 - Held, yes [Para 5] [In favour of assessee]GST: Construction service provided by applicant contractor under project 'La-Riveria', which is an affordable housing project, qualifies for application of lower rate of CGST of 6 per cent and SGST of 6 per cent w.e.f. 25-1-2018 as provided in Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended vide Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018

FACT: The applicant has been undertaking development of residential project 'La-Riveria'. The apartments in project La-Riveria are less than 60 sq. mt. RERA carpet area.

It seeks ruling on application of GST on said services.

HELD: The applicant has not been given the entire contract for construction of complete houses. Probably the carpentry work like making of doors, etc., electrical work, etc., does not seem to have been given to them. However, the job alloted to them are pertaining to affordable housing since each of the apartments is less than 60 sq. mtrs. Entry (V)(da) of Notification 1/2018, nowhere restricts the benefit to a 'developer' only. The Notification entry is qua the supply of service and not qua the person and, therefore, once a project qualifies as an Affordable Housing Project (AHP), the benefit of concessional rate of tax would be available in respect of works contract services pertaining to Low Cost Houses, irrespective of it being supplied by the developer or the contractor. Hence, in view of the above discussion and facts on record the applicant's case is covered under the tax rate of 12 per cent, under Heading 9954 (Construction Services), (V)(da) of abovementioned Notification No. 11/2017, as amended since the project undertaken by them falls under the definition of 'Affordable Housing' as also claimed by them in their application. The benefit of reduced rate would be available to them only in the case of supply effected after 25-1-2018, i.e., the date on which Notification 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate) was issued and the benefit of this reduced rate would be applicable in case of only those flats which are of carpet area upto 60 sq. mtrs., in this scheme, which is covered in the category of affodable housing. [Para 5]

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - A charitable organisation 'S' engaged in various charitable activities across Kerala has awarded a rehabilitation project to applicant for providing affordable shelter to 2018 flood victims - Applicant constructed 45 residential units in different locations on land belonging to flood victims identified by Trust - Whether activity undertaken by applicant cannot be construed as construction of affordable residential apartments by a promoter in a residential real estate project intended for sale to a buyer and, hence, rate of GST prescribed under Sl. No. 3(i) of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, is not applicable in respect of said activity - Held, yes - Whether activity undertaken by applicant is construction of 45 individual residential houses at different locations on land belonging to individual beneficiaries and activity squarely falls within scope of works contract as defined in section 2(119) - Held, yes - Whether services provided by applicant to 'S' for construction of low cost housing units falls within ambit of Sl. No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and is liable to GST at rate of 12 per cent - Held, yes [Paras 11 and 15]GST : Where applicant constructed residential units on land belonging to flood victims under a rehabilitation project awarded to it by a charitable trust, activity squarely falls within scope of works contract under section 2(119) and is liable to GST at rate of 12 per cent as per Sl. No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

FACT: The applicant is a non-governmental organization in the shelter sector having sustainable building solutions and green and humane architecture.

It is providing services in the field of construction of residences and affordable housing, architectural advisory services, execution of government contracts etc. with special focus on environment friendly construction.

A charitable organisation 'S' engaged in various charitable activities across Kerala has awarded a rehabilitation project to the applicant for providing affordable shelter to the 2018 flood victims.

The applicant is awarded the work of construction of 45 residential units ad-measuring approximately equal to or less than 450 Square feet in different locations each along with residential facilities on the land belonging to the flood victims identified by the Trust. The applicant shall design the houses, obtain the statutory permits and construct the houses and hand them over on a turnkey basis.

The applicant has sought advance ruling on the question as to whether the services provided by the applicant to 'S' for construction of low cost housing units for flood-affected individuals in Kerala fall within the ambit of Serial Number 3 (i), (v) or (va) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 03/2019 Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 and whether services by the applicant are otherwise exempt from whole or part of GST leviable thereon by Notification 12/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended.

HELD: The rate of GST prescribed under Sl. No. 3(i) of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 applies to construction of affordable residential apartments by a promoter in a residential real estate project intended for sale to a buyer except where the entire consideration is received after issuance of completion certificate. Further, the rate under this entry applies where the supply of the services involves transfer of land or undivided share of land and its value is included in the amount charged from the buyer. [Para 8]

The activity undertaken by the applicant for 'S' as per the agreement dated 16-11-2019 cannot by any stretch of imagination be construed as construction of affordable residential apartments by a promoter in a residential real estate project intended for sale to a buyer and, hence, the rate of GST prescribed under Sl. No. 3(i) of the Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 03/2019 Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 is not applicable in respect of the activity. The activity undertaken by the applicant is construction of 45 individual residential houses at different locations on the land belonging to the individual beneficiaries and the activity squarely falls within the scope of works contract as defined in section 2(119). [Para 11]

HEADNOTE: Section 171 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Anti-profiteering measure - Applicant filed application alleging profiteering by respondent in respect of purchase of a flat in respondent's project 'Habitat-78' - Applicant alleged that GST rate was reduced from 12 per cent to 8 per cent in terms of Notification No. 1/2018 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 in case of affordable housing projects but respondent charged GST at rate of 12 per cent and also failed to pass benefit of Input Tax Credit (ITC) - Whether since project was launched only after implementation of GST, there was no comparative pre-GST input tax credit (ITC) that was accumulated or utilized by respondent and, therefore, question of profiteering did not arise - Held, yes - Whether since respondent had charged GST at reduced rate of 8 per cent, respondent had not contravened provisions of section 171 - Held, yes [Paras 14, 15, 16  17][In favour of assessee]GST: Where project of construction of flats was launched after implementation of GST, there was no comparative pre-GST ITC that was accumulated or utilized by respondent-builder and, therefore, question of profiteering did not arise

FACT: The applicant filed application alleging profiteering by the respondent in respect of purchase of a flat in the respondent's project 'Habitat-78'.

The applicant had alleged that the respondent had charged 12 per cent GST on the demand raised on 17-4-2018, i.e., after 25-1-2018, when the GST rate was reduced from 12 per cent to 8 per cent in case of affordable housing projects and also that the benefit of Input Tax Credit (ITC) had not been passed on to her by the respondent by way of commensurate reduction in price.

The DGAP submitted that based on the respondent's replies the project 'Habitat-78' was not in existence before the implementation of GST and was launched only in the GST regime and the agreement with the applicant was also executed on 17-11-2017. The DGAP on scrutiny of the documents (Home buyer's list and Agreement with the applicant dated 17-11-2017) submitted by the respondent, found that there was no price history of the units sold in the pre-GST era which could be compared with the post-GST base price to determine whether there was any profiteering or not. The Report also stated that the draw of lots, allotment of units and receipt of payments had taken place post-GST and the construction also commenced in January, 2018 and, therefore, there was no pre-GST tax rate of ITC which could be compared with the post-GST tax rate and ITC. The DGAP's Report also stated that the respondent must have taken into consideration the benefit of ITC available to him post implementation of GST, while fixing the base price. The Report had further claimed that the respondent had reduced the GST rate from 12 per cent to 8 per cent with effect from 25-1-2018, in terms of Notification No. 01/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018. Therefore, the DGAP in his report had concluded that the provisions of section 171 would not be attracted.

FACT: The applicant, a Central Government Department, awarded a works contract to Tata Projects Ltd. for design, fabrication, procurement, instrumentation and control and commissioning of Trisonic Wind Tunnel with Ejector System. The work involves fabrication of machineries, transportation of equipments to be attached to the system, construction of civil structure where the machinery is to be installed. It sought advance ruling in respect of the following question:

If the above supply is considered as works contract, whether it would be covered under Entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 24/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017 attracting GST at the rate of 12 per cent.

HELD: Being a works contract awarded by the Central Government Department by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, of a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry or any other business or profession will attract 12 per cent GST as per Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. [Para 3]

Ruling

The work of design, realisation, integration and commissioning of Trisonic Wind Tunnel as a turnkey project will fall under the definition of works contract under section 2(119) of the CGST Act, 2017.

The service provided to the applicant by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out of a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession will attract 12 per cent GST as per Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. [Para 4]

The Floor Area Ratio (FAR), also known as the Floor Space Ratio (FSR) or the Floor Space Index (FSI), depicts the relationship between the total usable floor space in a building and the total area of the plot on which the building is constructed. In mathematical terms, FAR = CA/LA, where CA = Constructed area or built-up area, and LA = Land area. [Para 4.8] According to the Project Plan submitted at the time of the hearing, FAR for the entire project is 2.749 after deducting from the total built-up area the common areas like lift-lobby, stair area etc. FAR for the affordable residential apartments in the project should, therefore, be atleast 1.375. The total plot size being 5627 sq. mtr., the built-up area for affordable residential apartments should atleast be 7734 sq. mtr. The built-up area for the affordable residential apartments, as identified by the architect, under the RREP is 7885 sq. mtr. (the calculation sheet is attached). The relevant FAR, therefore, comes out to be 1.401, which is 50.96 per cent of the FAR for the project. The RREP, therefore, is an affordable housing project in terms of the AHP Notification. [Para 4.9]

Thus, it is concluded that the works contract service for the construction of those dwelling units in the RREP that are affordable residential apartments in terms of clause (xvi) of Paragraph 4 of the Rate Notification are taxable under Entry No. 3(v)(da) of the said notification, provided the applicant does not opt for paying tax at the rate specified in (ie) or (if) of Entry No. 3. [Para 4.10]

Thus, the works contract service for the construction of those dwelling units in the project named 'Akriti' that are affordable residential apartments in terms of clause (xvi) of Paragraph 4 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended from time-to-time, are taxable under Entry No. 3(v)(da) of the said notification, provided the applicant does not opt for paying tax at the rate specified in Entry No. 3(ie) or 3(if). [Para 4.10]

Moreover, the Government of Andhra Pradesh is reimbursing the money for agricultural services to the contractee on behalf of the customers. Therefore, the works executed are to a business entity by the applicant. The contractee is not rendering any non-commercial services inasmuch as they are getting reimbursed for their commercial activity on behalf of their customers. Therefore, this situation cannot be called as non-commercial at no stretch of imagination. The works undertaken by APEPDCL are for business purpose and the benefit of concessional rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent under Central tax and 6 per cent State tax) are any other concessional rate is not available to the applicant.

As per section 2 of CGST Act, 2017 and APGST Act, 2017 defines 'works contract' as a contract for building, construction, fabrication, completion, erection, installation, fitting out, improvement, modification, repair, maintenance, renovation, alteration or commissioning of any immovable property wherein transfer of property in goods (whether as goods or in some other form) is involved in the execution of such contract.

The composite supply of works contract as defined at section 2 of CGST Act, 2017 and APGST Act, 2017 is treated as supply of service in terms of Sl. No. 6, Schedule II of CGST Act, 2017 and APGST Act, 2017.

In the instant case, the contract entered by the applicant squarely falls under the works contract and falls under entry No. (ii) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended from time to time and corresponding notifications under APGST Act, 2017, and the applicable rate of tax is 18 per cent (9 per cent under Central tax and 9 per cent State tax).

The applicant is not entitled for the benefit of concessional rate of GST at the rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent under Central tax and 6 per cent State tax) for the stated works executed, in terms of Notification No. 24/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017, read with Notification No. 31/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017, or any other concessional rate. The applicable rate of tax is 18 per cent (9 per cent under Central tax and 9 per cent State tax) for the services referred by the applicant.

Whether a particular person is a Governmental authority or a Governmental Entity is to be decided in terms of the definition given in the Notification No. 31/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017 by applying the facts of each case.

Neither the contractee nor the stated works executed are 'non-commercial' in the facts and circumstances and the said stated works are taxable under GST. [Para 6]

HELD: The question is whether the transaction is covered under Sl. No. 3(vi) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.[Para 7.4]

As per entry No.3(vi) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, composite supply of works contract as defined in section 2(119) of the CGST Act, 2017, provided to the Government Entity by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession is liable to tax at the rate of 6 per cent under the CGST Act. Similar notification also exists under the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act and also under the Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act (wherein the tax rate is 12 per cent IGST).[Para 7.5]

The applicant is undertaking a contract of works contract of construction of a civil structure or any other original works for the Airport Authorities of India. The Department of Personnel and Training, Government of India has shown in the company profile that the shareholding of the Government of India in the Airport Authorities of India is 100 per cent and hence the AAI is a Government Entity.[Para 7.6]

Classification of services - Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Civil construction services - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Applicant-company is engaged in business of civil construction of residential premises as a contractor - It seeks advance ruling on issue as to whether construction services proposed to be provided by applicant will qualify for reduced GST rate of 12 per cent as provided in Sr. No. 3, item (v)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018-Central tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 - Low cost houses in an affordable housing project having area of 60 sq. mts. or upto 60 sq. mts. will attract 12 per cent GST - Whether since project undertaken by applicant is an affordable housing project, it will attract rate of 12 per cent GST under Sr. No. 3 of said Notification – Held, yes [Para 5.8][In favour of assessee]GST: Where applicant undertook project of construction of residential flat (Low cost flats) having carpet area of upto or less than 60 sq. mts. and its project falls under definition of 'Affordable Housing Project', applicant's case is covered under concessional tax rate slab of 12 per cent

Classification of services - Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Housing Project construction -  Heading 9954 - [Construction services] - Applicant has entered into civil construction contract with 'J' Ltd. in respect of seven residential buildings - Whether since project undertaken by applicant falls under definition of 'Affordable Housing Project' (carpet area being less than 60 sq. Mts.) applicant's case is covered under concessional tax rate of 12 per cent under Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) in terms of item (v)(da) of Sr. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017, Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, benefit of reduced rate would be available to applicant in cases of supply effected after 25-1-2018, i.e. date on which Notification 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate) was issued for those flats having carpet area upto 60 sq. mtrs. - Held, yes - Whether, however, in case of other flats which have carpet area more than 60 sq. mtrs. or which are commercial units, applicant would be required to pay GST at normal applicable rate - Held, yes - Whether building completion and finishing services will not be regarded as a separate services; such building completion and finishing services will be a part of composite supply of works contract services with principal supply of building construction - Held,yes - Whether 'housing project' cannot be confined only to dwelling units, it would also include within its fold, other common amenities, structures, etc. and, thus, rate applicable to principal supply will also be applicable to common amenities - Held, yes - Whether rate of GST will be 18% on works contract services provided for construction of units, common areas and amenities which do not qualify criteria of low cost houses - Held, yes [Paras 5.11, and 5.14.2][In favour of assessee]GST : Where applicant constructs residential complex under contract and project undertaken by it falls under definition of ‘affordable housing project’ (carpet area being less than 60 sq. Mts.), applicant’s case is covered under Heading No. 9954 eligible for concessional tax rate of 12 per cent; in case of other flats which have carpet area more than 60 sq. mtrs. or which are commercial units, applicant would be required to pay GST at normal applicable rate

Residential apartment construction - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 - Concessional Rate - Applicant-real estate developer has purchased land in its name and has obtained building permit - It has entered into two agreements with customers; one for sale of undivided share of land and another for construction of apartment - GST is not collected on amount collected for undivided share of land but same was collected for apartment construction at rate of 18 per cent - Applicant's project is satisfying all conditions of definition of 'ongoing project' as occurring in clause (xx) of Para 4 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 3/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 - Applicant is eligible and has exercised its option for continuing with payment of tax at old rates in respect of ongoing projects - Project is not covered under any of schemes specified under Item (ie) of Sl. No. 3 of said notification - Therefore, applicant is not eligible for concessional rate of tax at 12 per cent - Applicant is liable to pay GST at rate of 18 per cent in respect of services of construction of residential apartments supplied by it [Kerala Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 7.10] [In favour of revenue]GST : Applicant-real estate developer having exercised its option for continuing with payment of tax at old rates in respect to its ongoing project of construction of residential apartments should pay GST at rate of 18 per cent; since project is not covered under any of schemes specified under Item (ie) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), applicant is not eligible for concessional rate of tax of 12 per cent  GST : Where applicant is providing construction of residential apartment services alongwith sale of an undivided share of land in arriving at taxable value of supply, applicant will be eligible to avail deduction of one-third of total amount (being deemed value of undivided share of land) charged for supply   GST : Provisions of section 13 of CGST, 2017 will apply to determination of time of supply of construction of residential apartments services

Classification of services - Construction services (NR) - Applicant is engaged in business of construction of residential and commercial complex - Applicant is undertaking development of residential apartments under a project called 'Prajapati Magnum' - Whether since project undertaken by applicant falls under definition of 'Affordable Housing', applicant's case is covered under tax rate of 12 per cent, under Heading 9954 (Construction Services) of Notification No. 11/2017 but benefit of reduced rate would be available to them only in cases of supply effected after 25-1-2018, i.e., date on which Notification 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate) was issued and benefit of this reduced rate would be applicable in case of only those flats which are of carpet area upto 60 sq. mtrs. - Held, yes [Paras 5 and 6]CGST: Where project 'Prajapati Magnum' undertaken by applicants falls under definition of Affordable Housing, GST at rate of 12 per cent will be leviable on construction of low cost houses with carpet area upto 60 sq. m.

Construction service - Tax liability - Rate - Sale of semi-finished structure and supply of completion of semi-finished structure - HELD: Agreements entered with prospective buyers separately for sale of semi-finished structure and supply of service of completion of semi-finished structure by way of providing construction service will be considered as non-severable agreement or single contract - GST at rate of 1 per cent and 5 per cent will be levied on affordable housing and other housing respectively without ITC - If contract is severable from initial agreement, then GST at rate of 18 per cent will be levied for such construction service [Section 9 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Telangana Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 7] [In favour of assessee]

Works contract service - Construction of employee quarters - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Whether execution of works contract service for construction of residential quarters for employees of Kudankulam Nuclear Power Project (KKNPP) which is unit of Nuclear Power Corporation India Limited (NPCIL) would be taxable at 12 per cent - HELD : Works contract service is provided as is evident from contract - NPCIL qualifies as government entity as it has been established under Department of Atomic Energy with 100 per cent equity held by Central Government - Work entrusted to NPCIL is to implement atomic power projects for generation of electricity - Construction of residential quarters for KKNPP cannot be construed as work in relation to work entrusted to NPCIL by Central Government in absence of any document providing for same - Impugned works contract service is not covered under entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT(R) and concessional rate of 12 per cent is not available - GST is payable at 18 per cent in terms of entry at Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT(R) - Concessional rate of 12 per cent will not be available even if service rendered is in relation to work entrusted by government entity as said term was omitted from 1-1-2022 [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 7.3, 7.4, 7.5, 8 and 10] [In favour of revenue]GST : Concessional rate of 12 per cent GST is not available to works contract service rendered to government entity when same is not in relation to work entrusted by government till 31-12-2021 and even otherwise after 1-1-2022 such activity is liable to GST of 18 per cent  GST : Advance ruling cannot be sought on questions that are purely procedural in nature

Anti-profiteering measures - Charging higher rate of GST - Affordable Housing Scheme - Respondent-assessee providing construction services under Affordable Housing Scheme had charged GST at rate of 12 per cent instead of 8 per cent from flat buyers/applicant-complainant as reduced by Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax(Rate), dated 25-1-2018 which amended Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax(Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Applicable tax on construction services during pre-GST period was 4.5 per cent (Service Tax at rate of 4.5 per cent) which was enhanced to 8 per cent in GST regime by virtue of Notifications ibid. - There being no rate reduction after coming into force GST with effect from 1-7-2017, charging of GST at wrong rate/enhanced rate from flat buyers/applicant-complainant did not fall under scope of profiteering under section 171 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Matter was to be referred jurisdictional authorities for necessary action under Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 [Section 171 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Madhya Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 129 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Madhya Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 2(xxix), 2(xxx) and 21]

Construction of Commercial apartments - Tax Liabilityon supply of construction of a complex, building civil structure or a part thereof, including, commercial apartments -Applicant is engaged in supplying services of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation or alteration of affordable and other than affordable residential apartments, non-affordable housing and commercial apartments under Real Estate project (REP) - Applicant seeks advance ruling on applicable GST Rate on supply of construction of a complex, building civil structure or a part thereof, including, commercial apartments (shops, offices, godowns etc) by a promoter in a REP other than RREP - Held:In instant case, it is clear that services provided by taxpayer clearly falls under notification No. 03/2019- CT (rate) dated 29.03.2019 - Therefore , applicant is liable to pay GST at rate of 18% [9% - CGST + 9% - SGST] in respect of services of construction of complex, building, civil structure or a part including commercial apartments (shops, offices, godowns etc.) as per entry at Item No. (if) of Notification No. 03/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29.03.2019, subject to conditions prescribed under said entry. [Section 9 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Rajasthan Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017][Para 11][In favour of assessee]

Classification of services - Madhya Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 - Applicant-company is engaged in carrying out works contract in relation to construction of road, bridges, buildings, and civil structures - A company (MPPGCL) owned by Government of Madhya Pradesh, floated a tender, for construction of some flats - Applicant raised bill for work completed at rate of 18 per cent GST to MPPGCL - However, MPPGCL is of opinion that in work under reference, applicable rate of GST should be 12 per cent by treating itself as a Government entity - Whether since Government of Madhya Pradesh has a 100 per cent shareholding in MPPGCL and is also exercising full control over activities of said company, MPPGCL qualifies to be called and termed as a 'Government Entity' for purpose of GST - Held, yes - Whether since construction activity does not have any relation to principal work of power generation entrusted by State Government to MPPGCL, works contract service of construction of residential quarters would attract GST at rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) in terms of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and Notification No. 11/2017-Madhya Pradesh Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [para 5] [In favour of respondent]GST: Where activity of construction of flats allotted by MPPGCL to applicant does not have any relation to principal work of power generation entrusted by State Government to MPPCGL, work contract service of construction of residential quarters would attract GST at rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST)

Construction service - Composite supply of Works contracts - Heading No. 9954 - Concessional rate - Applicant is awarded construction services contract by Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation Ltd (APIIC) deriving its sustenance from sale of sheds, land, houses on outright sale or hire purchase - 100% of APIIC shares held by Andhra Pradesh Government and its nominees - HELD: APIIC is 'Government Entity' for GST matters as defined in para 4 of clauses (ix) and (x) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by  Notification No. 31/2017-CT (Rate) dated 13-10-2017 - However, APIIC runs on business model as it would pass on costs in its transactions to end client, and its activities and modus operandi are basically business and not otherwise - As construction is for APIIC's use to conduct its essentially business oriented activities, applicant's contract is not eligible for concessional rate of 12% under SI.No.3 (vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Applicant's contract is classifiable under SAC heading No. 9954 under Construction Services, with entry Sr. No. 3(ii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 i.e., Composite Supply of works contract as defined in section 2 (119) of CGST Act, 2017 and applicant is liable to 18 per cent rate of tax [Section 2(9) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Andhra Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 7] [In favour of revenue]GST : Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation Ltd (APIIC), whose 100% shares are held by Andhra Pradesh Government, is 'Government Entity' for GST matters; however, APIIC's activities being essentially business oriented and it passes its transaction costs to its end clients, applicant who is awarded construction contract by APIIC is not eligible for 12% concessional rate; it will be liable to 18% GST

II. Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Applicant entered into a contract with developer for construction of residential apartment - Applicant has not provided any evidence to effect that above project is covered under affordable housing project in terms of Sl. No. 3(v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Whether if projects are affordable housing projects and are given infrastructure status as per notification of Government of India, contract of supply by applicant would be covered under Entry No. 3(v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and liable to tax at rate of 6 per cent CGST and at 6 per cent SGST and, otherwise said services will be liable to tax at rate of 9 per cent under CGST Act and at rate of 9 per cent under KGST Act as provided in Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Para 14]

Classification of services - Haryana Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction of Affordable Group Housing Colony - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Applicant is engaged in development of commercial properties - It launched an Affordable Housing Project (Affordable Group Housing Colony) in Gurugram on 1-12-2015 under scheme approved by Government of Haryana (Affordable Housing Policy, 2013) and started construction of flats over land measuring 5 acres before 31-3-2019 - Assessee further submitted an application to Directorate of Town  Country Planning, Haryana on 3-2-2018 for grant of license for setting up another Affordable Group Housing Colony over land measuring 4 acres - It started construction of flats over land measuring 4 acres after 1-4-2019 - Whether project over said land is an ongoing project as construction was started before 31-3-2019 and, therefore, rate of tax applicable in respect of flats over said land is 12 per cent (with input tax credit + land abatement) in view of Notification No. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017 as applicant submitted an option to pay GST at old effective rate of 8 per cent and 12 per cent with input tax credit - Held, yes - Whether project over land measuring 4 acres is not an ongoing project as per Notification No. 3/2019 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 and applicable rate of tax on flats over said land is 0.5 per cent + 0.5 per cent (without input tax credit) - Held, yes [Paras 6.1 and 6.2] [In favour of applicant]GST : Where applicant launched an Affordable Housing Project (Affordable Group Housing Colony) in Gurugram under scheme approved by Government of Haryana (Affordable Housing Policy, 2013) and started construction of flats over land before 31-3-2019, project over said land is an ongoing project as construction was started before 31-3-2019 and, therefore, rate of tax applicable in respect of flats is 12 per cent (with input tax + land abatement) in view of Notification No. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017 as applicant submitted an option to pay GST at old effective rate of 8 per cent and 12 per cent with input tax credit

RBF shed construction - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 - Concessional rate - Construction services is being provided by applicant to Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation Ltd. (APIIC) - APIIC is getting revenue from operations like sale of land, houses, interest on hire purchase, long-term borrowings etc. - In APIIC, Andhra Pradesh Government and its nominees have 100 per cent shareholding, hence, it is "Government entity" as defined in para 4 of clauses (ix) and (x) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - APIIC derives its sustenance from sale of sheds, land, houses on outright sale or hire purchase etc. - APIIC runs on business model as it would pass costs in its transactions to end client - APIIC's activities are essentially business oriented - Hence, construction services provided by applicant to APIIC are not eligible for concessional rate of 12 per cent available under Notification No. 24/2017-CT (Rate), dated 21-9-2017 - Applicant's contract with APIIC is classifiable under Heading No. 9954 under construction services, with Entry No. (ii) of Sr. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 i.e., Composite Supply of Works Contract as defined in section 2(119) of CGST Act 2017 and APGST Act, 2017, and liable to 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST and 9 per cent SGST) [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Andhra Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 7] [In favour of revenue]GST : Even though APIIC is a Government entity, since its activities are essentially business oriented, RBF shed construction services as provided by applicant to APIIC are not eligible for concessional rate of 12 per cent GST; applicant's service would be classifiable under heading No. 9954; it is Composite Supply of Works Contract liable to 18 per cent GST

Works contract service to government entity - IT tower construction - Heading No. 9954 - Concessional rate - Service recipient is wholly owned by Government of Telangana and it qualifies as Government entity - Works contract services provided to government entity is subject to GST of 12 per cent in terms of entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax(Rate) - Memorandum of Association of Telangana State Infrastructure Corporation (TSIIC) states that company pursues objectives to implement incentive schemes formulated by Government of Telangana - IT towers constructed are meant for commerce/industry or any other business - Works contract service by way of construction of IT towers for TSIIC falls under exception to entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax(R) as structure is meant for commerce/industry or any other business - GST is payable at 18 per cent on works contract service provided [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Telangana Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 7] [In favour of revenue]GST : Concessional GST rate of 12 per cent is not applicable on works contract service of construction of IT towers for Government entity as it is meant for commerce/industry; GST is payable at 18 per cent

Hotel -cum-shopping and multiplex construction - Construction Services - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Applicant intends to get a land from WBHIDCO on 99 years lease for purpose of setting up of hotel-cum-shopping and multiplex which includes permission to construct certain area as residential flats - According to Draft Lease Deed as per tender, lessee is not permitted to sub-lease land or part thereof - However, applicant, being lessee, will be permitted to sub-lease/ assign right on constructed area - It is obvious that ownership of land remains with WBHIDCO - Applicant may sub-lease/assign rights of constructed area in following two models (a) one-time lump sum payment (may be payable in installments till completion and granting possession and registry in favour of prospective clients) for constructed units, (b) against periodic payments for use constructed area, during term of agreement, without any registry with Registrar and on expiry constructed area shall be repossessed by lessee i.e. applicant - HELD: Applicable SAC Code on this supply is 9954 as Construction Services) and applicable tax rate on supply under consideration shall be 18% - Applicant is eligible for a deduction as attributable to land portion i.e. 1/3 of consideration on total value of supply for purpose of payment of applicable tax - GST is to be paid on construction work for prospective clients, regardless of whether a lump sum or periodic payments, is charged [Section  9 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/ West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12] [In favour of Revenue] Hotel -cum-shopping and multiplex - Accomodation Service - Heading 9963 - Exemption - Applicant intends to get a land from WBHIDCO on 99 years lease for purpose of setting up of hotel-cum-shopping and multiplex which includes permission to construct certain area as residential flats - According to Draft Lease Deed as per tender, lessee is not permitted to sub-lease land or part thereof - However, applicant, being lessee, will be permitted to sub-lease/ assign right on constructed area - It is obvious that ownership of land remains with WBHIDCO - Applicant may sub-lease/assign rights of constructed area in following two models (a) one-time lump sum payment (may be payable in installments till completion and granting possession and registry in favour of prospective clients) for constructed units, (b) against periodic payments for use constructed area, during term of agreement, without any registry with Registrar and on expiry constructed area shall be repossessed by lessee i.e. applicant - HELD: - It will not fall under Accommodation Service under SAC Code 9963 and, hence, question of exemption under entry in sl. No. 12 of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated June 28, 2017 does not arise [Section  11 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/ West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 3.12] [In favour of Revenue] Hotel - Membership Organization Services - Heading No. 9995 - Classification - Applicant intends to get a land from WBHIDCO on 99 years lease for purpose of setting up of hotel-cum-shopping and multiplex which includes permission to construct certain area as residential flats - According to Draft Lease Deed as per tender, lessee is not permitted to sub-lease land or part thereof - However, applicant, being lessee, will be permitted to sub-lease/ assign right on constructed area - It is obvious that ownership of land remains with WBHIDCO - Applicant may sub-lease/assign rights of constructed area in following two models (a) one-time lump sum payment (may be payable in installments till completion and granting possession and registry in favour of prospective clients) for constructed units, (b) against periodic payments for use constructed area, during term of agreement, without any registry with Registrar and on expiry constructed area shall be repossessed by lessee i.e. applicant - Besides above arrangement, prospective customers may also be required to pay monthly/annual maintenance charges either directly toapplicant or to some society made for same - HELD: GST is payable on monthly/annual maintenance charges as per entry in sl. no. 33 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated June 28, 2017 - SAC Code in this case would be 9995 and the applicable GST rate is 18% [Section  9 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/ West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 3.12] [In favour of revenue]   Circulars and Notifications: Notification No. 11/2017 dated 28-6-2017, Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated June 28, 2017

Works contract service - Services provided to government entity - IT tower construction - Heading No. 9954 - Concessional rate - Service recipient Telangana State Infrastructure Corporation Limited (TSIIC) is wholly owned by Government of Telangana and qualifies as government entity - Works contract services provided to government entity is subject to GST of 12 per cent in terms of entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) - Memorandum of Association of TSIIC states that company pursues objectives to implement incentive schemes formulated by Government of Telangana - IT towers constructed are meant for commerce/industry or any other business - Works contract service by way of construction of IT towers for TSIIC falls under exception to entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT(R) as structure is meant for commerce/industry or any other business - GST is payable at 18 per cent on works contract service provided [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Telangana Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 7] [In favour of revenue]GST : Concessional GST rate of 12 per cent is not applicable on works contract service of construction of IT towers for government entity as it is meant for commerce/industry; GST is payable at 18 per cent
