(Rate), dated 28-6-2017, Notification No. 24/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 21-9-2017, Notification No. 17/2018-C.T. (Rate), dated 26-7-2018,  Notification No. 31/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 13-10-2017

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Heading No. 9954 [Construction Services] - Applicant a Private Limited Company entered into a works contract agreement with National Centre for Biological Sciences(NCBS) for construction of Hostel building at NCBS Campus in Bangalore - It sought advance ruling on whether it should charge GST at rate of 12 per cent for service provided to NCBS as per Notification No 24/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 21-9-2017- It is found that NCBS, which is a separate centre of Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), receives grant from Department of Atomic Energy, Government of India and that NCBS is neither set-up by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature nor was established by any Government, but is an autonomous body under aegis of TIFR - Moreover, council administering this institute has only 4 members appointed by Government and therefore Government does not have more than 90 per cent control over it - Thus, NCBS is not covered under definition of a 'Government Entity' as per clause (x) of para 4 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax(Rate) dated 28-6-2017 - Furthermore, Institute is not established to carry out a function entrusted by Government, thus, it is not covered by clause (vi) of serial no. 3 of Notification - Whether therefore, service supplied by applicant to NCBS is not taxable at concessional rate of 12 per cent and is taxable at 18 per cent under residual item no. (xii) of Serial No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Paras 5 and 6]GST: Works contract service provided by applicant to National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS) for construction of hostel building on campus is taxable at 18 per cent GST under residual item no. (xii) of Serial No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017

Emoluments paid to staff - Other employment and labour supply services nowhere else classified - Heading No. 998519 - Classification - Tax Liability - Applicant is authority created under Airports Authority of India Act, 1994 - Applicant entered into a concessionaire agreement with Adani Thiruvananthapuram International Airport Limited - Applicant seeks advance ruling on whether GST is leviable on invoice raised by applicant staff cost salary/of reimbursement Thiruvananthapuram International Airport Limited? If yes, at what rate? - Held: From clause 6.5.5 of agreement, impugned amount represents 'emoluments' payable by applicant to select employees, i.e., employees of applicant working for concessionaire - In this regard, employees of applicant are supplied to concessionaire for a consideration, in pursuant to agreement - Hence, this service falls under 'Other employment and labour supply services nowhere else classified' viz. HSN 998519 - Applicable tax rate for this SAC is 9 per cent each towards CGST and SGST as applicable vide Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. [Section 9 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 8] [Against assessee]

Government Housing Scheme - Construction services -  Composite supply of work contract - Heading No. 9954 -Applicant-assessee is engaged in construction services - It has undertaken works contract tendered by Rajasthan Housing Board under scheme of Chief Minister Jan Awas Yojna 2015 programme having nexus with 'Housing for all' initiative under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojna of Government of India - HELD: As per Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022, GST rates of works contract involving construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration rendered to Government or Local authority is increased to 18 per cent - In light of Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022, services provided by applicant to RHB will attract a rate of 18 per cent GST after 13-7-2022 onward until rate is not changed [Section 9 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Rajasthan Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 6 and 7] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where applicant, engaged in providing construction services, undertook work contract tendered by Rajasthan Housing Board under scheme of Chief Minister Jan Awas Yojna 2015, services provided by assessee will attract a rate of 18 per cent GST as per Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022

Fire-fighting installation with pump house -  Construction of a complex, building, civil structure or a part thereof, including a complex or building intended for sale to a buyer, wholly or partly - Heading No. 9954 - Exemption - Appellant-assessee is a partnership firm and a civil contractor engaged in construction of roads, buildings, civil structures or various other civil works as awarded from various Governmental and non-Governmental organizations - AAR has held that appellant, is liable to pay GST at rate 18 per cent - What will be GST rate for work undertaken by appellant for service recipient under bid - HELD : It is observed that services provided by appellant are covered under Item number (vi) in Column (3) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended - Therefore, said services are liable to attract GST at 12 per cent (i.e. 6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent SGST) during contracted period only up to 31-12-2021, as after that, in Column No. (3) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 words 'Governmental authority or a Government entity' has been omitted vide Notification No. 22/2021-Central Tax(Rate), dated 31-12-2021 with effect from 1-1-2022 [Section 11 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Rajasthan Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para11] [Partly in favour of assessee]

Works contract services - Government entity - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Karnataka Residential Educational Institutions Society (KRIES) is formed under societies Registration Act and Government of Karnataka may appoint persons to review progress of society and to hold inquiries into affairs of society and give directions; hence, qualifies to be considered as a Government Entity - Works contract services executed for Construction of Residential school complex are liable to GST at 18 per cent with effect from 1-1-2022 as per Entry No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended vide Notification No. 22/2021-Central Tax (Rate), dated 31-12-2021 and Notification No. 03/2022 - Central Tax (Rate), dated : 13-7-2022 [Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10.3 and 14] [In favour of revenue]

Classification of services - Madhya Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction of residential quarters - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Applicant (M.P. Power Generating Co. Ltd.) is 100 per cent Madhya Pradesh State Government hold company - State Government of Madhya Pradesh awarded a contract to applicant to construct a Thermal Power Project - Further applicant awarded a contract to one 'S' towards construction of certain residential quarters at Thermal Power Project - Whether work contract awarded by applicant to 'S' for construction of residential quarters at Thermal Power Project shall attract GST at rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) under Heading No. 9954 - Held, yes [Para 8.1][In favour of revenue]GST: Where State Government of Madhya Pradesh awarded a contract to applicant, a 100 per cent State Government hold company, to construct a Thermal Power Project and further applicant awarded a contract to one 'S' towards construction of certain residential quarters at Thermal Power Project, work contract awarded by applicant to 'S' for construction of residential quarters shall attract GST at rate of 18 per cent under Heading No. 9954

Government Housing Scheme - Construction services -  Composite supply of work contract - Heading No. 9954 -Applicant-assessee is engaged in construction services - It has undertaken works contract tendered by Rajasthan Housing Board under scheme of Chief Minister Jan Awas Yojna 2015 programme having nexus with 'Housing for all' initiative under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojna of Government of India - HELD: As per Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022, GST rates of works contract involving construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration rendered to Government or Local authority is increased to 18 per cent - In light of Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022, services provided by applicant to RHB will attract a rate of 18 per cent GST after 13-7-2022 onward until rate is not changed [Section 9 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Rajasthan Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 6 and 7] [In favour of assessee]   Circulars and Notifications: Notification No. 3/2022- Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022.

Hotel -cum-shopping and multiplex construction - Construction Services - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Applicant intends to get a land from WBHIDCO on 99 years lease for purpose of setting up of hotel-cum-shopping and multiplex which includes permission to construct certain area as residential flats - According to Draft Lease Deed as per tender, lessee is not permitted to sub-lease land or part thereof - However, applicant, being lessee, will be permitted to sub-lease/ assign right on constructed area - It is obvious that ownership of land remains with WBHIDCO - Applicant may sub-lease/assign rights of constructed area in following two models (a) one-time lump sum payment (may be payable in installments till completion and granting possession and registry in favour of prospective clients) for constructed units, (b) against periodic payments for use constructed area, during term of agreement, without any registry with Registrar and on expiry constructed area shall be repossessed by lessee i.e. applicant - HELD: Applicable SAC Code on this supply is 9954 as Construction Services) and applicable tax rate on supply under consideration shall be 18% - Applicant is eligible for a deduction as attributable to land portion i.e. 1/3 of consideration on total value of supply for purpose of payment of applicable tax - GST is to be paid on construction work for prospective clients, regardless of whether a lump sum or periodic payments, is charged [Section  9 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/ West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12] [In favour of Revenue]GST : Where applicant gets a land on 99 years lease, sets up hotel-cum-shopping and multiplex and sub-leases constructed area, applicable SAC Code on this supply is 9954 (Construction Services) and applicable tax rate on supply under consideration shall be 18%  GST: Where applicant gets a land on 99 years lease, sets up hotel-cum-shopping and multiplex and sub-leases constructed area, such service will not fall under Accommodation Service (SAC: 9963) and, hence, question of exemption under entry in sl. No. 12 of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) will not arise  GST: Where applicant gets a land on 99 years lease, sets up hotel-cum-shopping and multiplex and sub-leases constructed area, monthly/annual maintenance charges will be liable to GST as per sl. no. 33 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate); SAC Code would be 9995 and applicable GST rate is 18%

Works contract service - Government entity - State Industrial Infrastructure Corporation TSIIC being wholly owned by Government of Telangana qualifies to be Government entity - TSIIC works to further policies of State Government, Central Government and Local Government for development of industries in State of Telangana - Construction of administrative building is not meant for commerce/industry or any other business - TSIIC has procured works contract service in relation to work entrusted to it by State Government - Construction of administrative building for TSIIC is taxable at 12 per cent GST - Works executed for Governmental authority or governmental entity from 1-1-2022 shall attract GST at 18 per cent as phrase 'Governmental authority or Governmental entity' is excluded as per amendments [Para 7] [In favour of applicant]GST : Concessional rate of 12 per cent GST on works contract is applicable on services provided to, state industrial infrastructure corporation wholly owned by State Government till 31-12-2021; GST at rate of 18 per cent is applicable to such services from 1-1-2022

Residential apartment construction - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 - Concessional Rate - Applicant-real estate developer has purchased land in its name and has obtained building permit - It has entered into two agreements with customers; one for sale of undivided share of land and another for construction of apartment - GST is not collected on amount collected for undivided share of land but same was collected for apartment construction at rate of 18 per cent - Applicant's project is satisfying all conditions of definition of 'ongoing project' as occurring in clause (xx) of Para 4 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 3/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 - Applicant is eligible and has exercised its option for continuing with payment of tax at old rates in respect of ongoing projects - Project is not covered under any of schemes specified under Item (ie) of Sl. No. 3 of said notification - Therefore, applicant is not eligible for concessional rate of tax at 12 per cent - Applicant is liable to pay GST at rate of 18 per cent in respect of services of construction of residential apartments supplied by it [Kerala Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 7.10] [In favour of revenue]  Valuation - Residential apartments - Applicant-real estate developer being service provider entered into two agreements with customers; one for sale of an undivided share of land and another for construction of apartment - In terms of paragraph 2 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, value of land or undivided share of land should be deemed to be one-third of total amount charged for supply irrespective of actual value of land - Accordingly, applicant is eligible to avail deduction of one-third of total amount charged for supply in arriving at taxable value of supply [Section 15 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Kerala Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 7.11.2 ] [In favour of assessee]  Construction of residential apartments - Time of supply - Provisions of section 13 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 will apply to determination of time of supply [Section 13 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 7.11.2]   Circulars and Notifications : Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, Notification No. 3/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 and Notification No. 6/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019

Construction service - Affordable residential apartment - Heading No. 9954 - Concessional rate - Residential Real Estate Project (RREP) comprised of both affordable and other than affordable residential apartments - HELD : Project undertaken is covered under definition of 'real estate project' and applicant falls within definition of a 'promoter' - Construction of affordable residential apartments is covered under services specified in entry at Sl. No. 3(i) and (ia) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) - GST is payable at 1.5 per cent in respect of service of construction of affordable residential apartments and at 7.5 per cent in respect of service of construction of residential apartments other than affordable residential apartments [Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 7.7 and 7.8] [In favour of assessee]   Circulars  Notifications : Notification No. 3/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 and Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

I. Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant entered into a contract with developer for construction of residential apartment - Whether since contract is for construction of an immovable property, same is covered under works contract as per section 2(119) - Held, yes [Para 12]GST : If projects are affordable housing projects and are given infrastructure status as per notification of Government of India, construction service provided by applicant to developer under residential project is liable to tax at rate of 6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent KGST as provided in Sl. No. 3(v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017; else, services will be liable to tax at rate of 9 per cent under CGST Act and at rate of 9 per cent under KGST Act as provided in Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017  GST : Where applicant, engaged in business of civil works contract entered into an agreement with developer for construction of residential apartment project, since contract is for construction of an immovable property, same is covered under works contract as per section 2(119)

Classification of services - Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - A charitable organisation 'S' engaged in various charitable activities across Kerala has awarded a rehabilitation project to applicant for providing affordable shelter to 2018 flood victims - Applicant constructed 45 residential units in different locations on land belonging to flood victims identified by Trust - Whether activity undertaken by applicant cannot be construed as construction of affordable residential apartments by a promoter in a residential real estate project intended for sale to a buyer and, hence, rate of GST prescribed under Sl. No. 3(i) of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, is not applicable in respect of said activity - Held, yes - Whether activity undertaken by applicant is construction of 45 individual residential houses at different locations on land belonging to individual beneficiaries and activity squarely falls within scope of works contract as defined in section 2(119) - Held, yes - Whether services provided by applicant to 'S' for construction of low cost housing units falls within ambit of Sl. No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and is liable to GST at rate of 12 per cent - Held, yes [Paras 11 and 15]GST : Where applicant constructed residential units on land belonging to flood victims under a rehabilitation project awarded to it by a charitable trust, activity squarely falls within scope of works contract under section 2(119) and is liable to GST at rate of 12 per cent as per Sl. No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

Construction Service - Rate of GST - Advance ruling is sought on question as to whether GST is to be charged at rate of 1.5% or at rate of 7.5% from customers for sale of flats - HELD: Project in present case commenced after 1-4-2019 - Registration was not taken as any affordable housing scheme of government - Affordable Housing Scheme as notified is applicable to projects that were on-going as on 1-4-2019 - Effective scheme is not applicable to present project as commencement is after said date - As instant project is satisfying criteria of affordable residential apartment as per Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), GST is payable at 1.5 per cent for sale of flats, except where entire consideration is received after issuance of completion certificate or after its first occupation, as reduced by 1/3rd to factor value of land [Para 4.18] [In favour of revenue]

Works contract service - Government entity - Heading No. 9954 - Concessional rate of tax - Applicant is engaged in providing works contract service to Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation Ltd. (APIIC) - HELD: APIIC qualifies as a 'Government entity' as Government of Andhra Pradesh including its nominees have 100 per cent of shareholding and same is evident from shareholding ratios mentioned in Annual Report - APIIC is engaged in business activities as construction work undertaken is meant for use by Ministry of Industries which is essentially meant for promotion of business and industry - Concessional rate of GST at 12 per cent is not available - Services provided to APIIC are in nature of composite supply of works contract service, classifiable under SAC 9954 and GST is payable at 18 per cent on same in terms of entry at SL. No. 3(ii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) [Andhra Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [In favour of revenue]GST : Construction service provided to APIIC is not eligible for GST at 12 per cent as APIIC, although qualifies as Government entity, is engaged in promotion of business and industry; GST is payable at 18 per cent on supply of services to APIIC

Construction Service - Hospital of government entity - Heading 9954 - Classification - Whether service of construction of 200 bedded hospital to be provided to Uttar Pradesh Rajkiya Nirman Nigam Ltd., (UPRNN) is eligible for concessional rate of GST at 12% in terms of S. No. 3 (vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) - Applicant is required to construct entire hospital for Employee State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) - Composite supply of works contract by way of construction of a hospital i.e., clinical establishment is provided to government entity - HELD : Service is eligible for concessional rate when they are provided to Union territory or local authority and is not eligible for concessional rate if provided to governmental authority or government entity as per amendment to Notification No. 11/2017 by Notification No. 15/2021 - Service to be provided is not covered under said entry of Notification No. 11/2017 providing for 12% GST rate and same will be covered under residuary clause (xii) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 attracting 18% GST [Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 5.2, 5.3.2, 5.3.3, 5.3.5, 5.4.1 and 5.4.2] [In favour of revenue]GST : Service of construction of hospital to be provided to a government entity is not covered under amended entry pertaining to concessional rate of 12% GST; such service attracts 18% GST

Residential house - Construction service - GST rate - Petitioner-allottee contended that 8 per cent GST rate specified by respondent-U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad was contrary to instructions issued by Ministry of Finance - Only dispute between parties was whether respondent State Avas Evam Vikas Parishad was entitled to charge GST at rate of 1 per cent or 8 per cent - Reference had been made to certain internal communications between authorities of respondent, rate of tax was to be charged as per notification issued under GST Act, 2017 - Therefore, said issue could not be adjudicated at preliminary stage, that too when dispute was brought by allottee against U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad - Respondent development authority was directed to ascertain correct GST rate from appropriate GST authority and communicate same to petitioners within three months [Section 9 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Uttar Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 3 and 4]   Circulars and Notifications : Instruction issued by Government of India, Ministry of Finance, dated 7-5-2019

Pure labour service - Construction service - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Applicant entered into an agreement with M/s B.C.M. Builders LLP to provide pure labour construction services - M/s B.C.M. Builders LLP has entered into a contract with Rajasthan Government to construct 380 flats under 'Affordable Housing Scheme under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana' (including material and labour) - M/s B.C.M. Builders LLP has further sublet work to applicant - HELD : As per Entry No. 10 of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), following main requirements to get the benefit of the above notification - (a) Services provided by way of pure labour contracts and (b) Applicable only to the beneficiary-led individual house construction or enhancement under the Housing for All (Urban) Mission or Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - As applicant is under obligation to provide machine and other material besides labour supply, agreement between applicant and M/s B.C.M. Builders LLP is not a pure labour contract service supplied for construction of 380 flats under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Further, benefit of relevant entry of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 is applicable only to beneficiary-led individual house construction or enhancement under Housing for All (Urban) Mission or Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Applicant could not establish that they are working for Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Therefore, service provided by applicant for construction of flats is not covered under Entry No. 10 of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 (as amended) - Construction service provided by applicant falls under HSN code 9954 attracting GST at rate of 18 per cent [Section  9 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/ Rajasthan Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 8 to 11] [In favour of revenue]

Works contract services - Government entity - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Kudala Sangama Development Board was established under Kudala Sangama Development Board Act, 1994 - More than 90 per cent of members of board are from State Government and all administrative expenses of board are covered by grants given by State Government; hence, it qualifies to be considered as a Government Entity - Works contract services executed for construction of International Center and Museum are liable to GST at 18 per cent with effect from 1-1-2022 as per entry No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended vide Notification No. 22/2021-Central Tax (Rate), dated 31-12-2021 and Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 [Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10.2 and 14] [In favour of revenue]

facts.text:
The applicant-company (MPPGCL) is engaged in carrying out the works contract in relation to construction of road, bridges, buildings, civil structures of Government, semi-Government and private undertakings.

The applicant was awarded a contract for construction of 599 flats by MPPGCL.

During the course of carrying out the construction work, the applicant company raised Running Bills (RA bills) for the portion of work completed at a point of time to MPPGCL by charging CGST and SGST at the rate of 9 per cent each, in view of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017.

MPPGCL is of the opinion that in the work under reference, the applicable rate of GST should be 12 per cent (6+6), as per Notification No.11/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017, by treating itself as a Government entity and the work allocated to the service provider is the work which is the work supplied to it by the Government.

The applicant seeks advance ruling on issue as to whether MPPGCL is a 'Government Entity' and whether the work contract service of construction of 599 residential quarters allotted to the applicant company, will be charged under the GST rate of 12 per cent (6+6) or 18 per cent (9+9).

The applicant has entered into civil construction contract with 'J' Ltd. in respect of seven residential buildings.

The applicant seeks advance ruling on question as to whether the construction services proposed to be provided by the applicant under the subject project will qualify for the reduced GST rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent each of CGST & SGST), as provided in Sl. No. 3, item (v), sub-item (da) of Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018.

The applicant-company is engaged in the business of civil construction of residential premises as a contractor. It had filed the instant application in respect of a proposed civil construction contract to be entered into with a developer for construction of a residential project comprising of 135 buildings all having residential flats/units having carpet area of up to or less than 60 Sq. Mts. According to them, since more than 50 per cent of PSI is utilized towards construction of LCH, the project would qualify as an 'Affordable Housing Project' (AHP).

It seeks advance ruling on the issue as to whether the construction services proposed to be provided by the applicant will qualify for the reduced CGST rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent each of CGST & SGST), as provided in Sr. No. 3, item (v)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018.

The applicant is engaged in development of commercial properties.

It launched an Affordable Housing Project [Affordable Group Housing Colony] in Gurugram on 1-12-2015 under the scheme approved by the Government of Haryana [Affordable Housing Policy, 2013]. For the construction of Affordable Group Housing Colony, it was granted License No. 11 of 2014, dated 10-6-2014 by the Town & Country Planning Department, Haryana on the land measuring 5 acres located in the Revenue Estate of Village Dhankot, Sector 102, Gurugram. The building plan for construction of affordable flats was approved on 26-3-2015. The applicant started construction of flats before 31-3-2019 and the booking in respect of flats was also made in the pre-GST period.

The applicant further submitted an application to the Directorate of Town & Country Planning, Haryana on 3-2-2018 for the grant of license for setting up another Affordable Group Housing Colony over the land measuring 4 acres located in the Revenue Estate of Village Dhankot, Sector 102, Gurugram.

A separate license bearing No. 82 of 2018 for the construction of flats on the said land was granted by the Town & Country Planning Department on 6-12-2018. The building plan in respect of the said project was approved on 27-5-2019. On the basis of License No. 82 of 2018, the applicant was granted license bearing No. GGM/339/339/71/2019/33, dated 27-5-2019 by the Real Estate Regulation Authority (RERA) for construction of 595 flats in six towers.

The applicant sought advance ruling on the following question:

Whether the applicant is to pay tax at the rate of 6 per cent + 6 per cent (after availing land abatement = 4 per cent + 4 per cent) availing the input tax and as provided under Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and Notification No. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 under Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and Notification No. 46/ST2, dated 30-6-2017 and Notification No. 74/ST2, dated 22-8-2017 under Haryana Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.

The applicant filed application alleging profiteering by the respondent in respect of purchase of a flat in the respondent's project 'Habitat-78'.

The applicant had alleged that the respondent had charged 12 per cent GST on the demand raised on 17-4-2018, i.e., after 25-1-2018, when the GST rate was reduced from 12 per cent to 8 per cent in case of affordable housing projects and also that the benefit of Input Tax Credit (ITC) had not been passed on to her by the respondent by way of commensurate reduction in price.

The DGAP submitted that based on the respondent's replies the project 'Habitat-78' was not in existence before the implementation of GST and was launched only in the GST regime and the agreement with the applicant was also executed on 17-11-2017. The DGAP on scrutiny of the documents (Home buyer's list and Agreement with the applicant dated 17-11-2017) submitted by the respondent, found that there was no price history of the units sold in the pre-GST era which could be compared with the post-GST base price to determine whether there was any profiteering or not. The Report also stated that the draw of lots, allotment of units and receipt of payments had taken place post-GST and the construction also commenced in January, 2018 and, therefore, there was no pre-GST tax rate of ITC which could be compared with the post-GST tax rate and ITC. The DGAP's Report also stated that the respondent must have taken into consideration the benefit of ITC available to him post implementation of GST, while fixing the base price. The Report had further claimed that the respondent had reduced the GST rate from 12 per cent to 8 per cent with effect from 25-1-2018, in terms of Notification No. 01/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018. Therefore, the DGAP in his report had concluded that the provisions of section 171 would not be attracted.

The applicant is engaged in works contract by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration.

The applicant is seeking Advance Ruling on questions as to what is rate of tax applicable to the composite supply of works contract as undertaken by the supplier (applicant) i.e., whether the GST rate 18 per cent or 12 per cent is to be charged by the supplier? and whether the amendment through Notification No. 20/2017 and 24/2017 to Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 wherein the GST rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) has been notified in respect of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 will be effective from the date of Notification No. 11/2017 and whether it would be in order for the applicant (supplier) to charge GST at the rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) or is the GST rate 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) applicable to the nature of works contract undertaken by the applicant?

The applicant-firm of builders and developers is desirous to undertake an affordable housing project in Kolhapur. The land required for the project is already possessed by the firm. The units to be constructed in the said project will be of upto 30 sq. mtrs. (EWS) or upto 60 sq. mtrs. (LIG). It seeks advance ruling as to what is the rate of tax to be levied on the sale of Flats/Units to the prospective buyers? and whether full ITC is allowable or it will be restricted to out put GST liability?

The respondent was executing an affordable Housing Scheme approved by the Government of Haryana under the name and style of 'Arawali Homes'.

An application was filed before the Haryana State Screening Committee on Anti-Profiteering alleging profiteering by the respondent in respect of purchase of a flat in the respondent's project 'Arawali Homes'. The applicant had alleged that the respondent was collecting wrong GST post-implementation of GST and was not refunding GST collected in the wrong manner, even after sending clarification that the GST was not applicable to 'Affordable Housing', as the GST amount could be adjusted against the Input Tax Credit (ITC).

The DGAP noted that the ITC as a percentage of the turnover that was available to the respondent during the pre-GST period from April, 2016 to June, 2017 was 2.42 per cent and during the post-GST period from July, 2017 to August, 2018, it was 10.70 per cent which clearly established that post-GST, the respondent had benefited from additional ITC to the tune of 8.28 per cent [10.70 per cent (-) 2.42 per cent] of the taxable turnover. The effective GST rate on construction service in respect of the affordable and low-cost houses upto a carpet area of 60 square metres was further reduced from 12 per cent to 8 per cent, vide Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018.

The applicant is providing works contract service as sub-contractor to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways. It executes and undertakes composite supply of works contract.

It sought advance ruling on the following questions:

1.

What tax rate to be charged by the applicant to main contractor on works contract services pertaining to railways original works contract.

2.

Whether to charge tax rate of 12 per cent GST or 18 per cent GST.

The Authority for Advance Rulings ruled that

-

The tax rate to be charged by the applicant to the main contractor would be at the rate of 6 per cent of CGST and 6 per cent of SGST.

-

The tax rate to be charged would be 12 per cent.

On appeal to Appellate Authority for Advance Ruling by revenue:

The appellant is having business of caterers and supplies food, beverages and other eatables (non-alcoholic drinks) complete services at various places of their customers, who have in house canteens of their factories.

The appellant submitted that it normally charges GST at the rate of 18 per cent classifying their services under heading 9963 as 'outdoor catering'.

The appellant submitted that one of the customers, who was recipient of services, had given the contract for catering services to be provided to the staff and premise for services to be provided for canteen, which was non air-conditioned, had also been made available to the appellant. The said customer had asked the appellant to charge GST at the rate of 12 per cent, therefore, the appellant requested for advance ruling as to whether rate of tax on their supplies made to the recipient would be 12 per cent or 18 per cent.

The Gujarat Authority for Advance Ruling ruled that the supply of services by appellant is covered under Sr. 7(v) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017, as amended, issued under the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and Notification No. 11/2017- Gujarat State Tax (Rate) dated 30-6-2017, as amended, issued under the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, attracting Goods and Service Tax at the rate of 18 per cent (CGST 9 per cent +SGST 9 per cent.

If the GST rate 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST+ 9 per cent SGST) as prescribed in serial No. 3, against heading No. 9954 (construction services), specified in Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, is the rate applicable to the nature of works contract undertaken by the applicant, kindly clarify the following related aspects also:

The applicant filed application before Anti-profiteering Authority alleging that the respondent had not passed on the benefit of input tax credit by way of commensurate reduction in price in respect of purchase of two flats in the respondent's project 'River View Heights'.

The DGAP concluded in his report that the input tax credit as a percentage of the total turnover that was available to the respondent during the pre-GST period (April, 2016 to June, 2017) was 2.37 per cent and during the post-GST period (July, 2017 to October, 2018), was 2.65 per cent which confirmed that post-GST, the respondent had benefitted from additional input tax credit to the tune of 0.28 per cent (2.65 per cent - 2.37 per cent) of the total turnover. Further, the DGAP had stated that the profiteering has been examined by comparing the applicable tax and input tax credit available for the pre-GST period (April, 2016 to June, 2017) when service tax at the rate of 4.5 per cent and VAT at the rate of 1 per cent was payable (total tax rate of 5.5 per cent) with the post-GST period (July, 2017 to October, 2018) when the effective GST rate was 12 per cent (GST at the rate of 18 per cent along with 1/3rd abatement on value) on construction service, which was fixed vide Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. On the basis of this, the DGAP had summarized the comparative figures of the applicable tax rate and ratio of input tax credit to the turnover during the pre-GST period and the post-GST period as well as had recaliberated the basic price and the excess realization (profiteering) during the post-GST period.

The DGAP further concluded that the amount of benefit of input tax credit not passed on to the recipients or in other words, the profiteered amount came to Rs. 2,13,468 which included 12 per cent GST on the base profiteering amount of Rs. 1,90,596, and the computation of profiteering was in respect of 26 home buyers from whom payments had been received by the respondent during the post-GST period from 1-7-2017 to 31-10-2018.

The applicant filed application before Anti-Profiteering Authority alleging profiteering by the respondent while he had purchased flat in the respondent's project 'Palm Wood Royal Gulmohar Green' in Mohan Nagar, Ghaziabad.

The applicant had also alleged that the respondent had not passed on the benefit of Input Tax Credit (ITC) although he had charged GST at the rate of 12 per cent with effect from 1-7-2017 from him.

The DGAP stated in his Report that the flat was booked by the applicant on 19-1-2017 before the GST had come into force with effect from 1-7-2017.

The DGAP stated that the ITC as a percentage of the total turnover that was available to the respondent during the pre-GST period from April, 2016 to June, 2017 was 3.23 per cent and during the post-GST period from July, 2017 to August, 2018 it was 6.52 per cent, which confirmed that post-GST, the respondent had benefited from the additional ITC to the tune of 3.29 per cent [6.52 per cent (-) 3.23 per cent] of the total turnover. Accordingly, the DGAP has assessed the amount of profiteering by comparing the applicable tax rates and the ITC available during the pre-GST period (April, 2016 to June, 2017) when Service Tax at the rate of 4.5 per cent with the post-GST period (July, 2017 to September, 2018) when the effective GST rate was 12 per cent (GST at the rate of 18 per cent along with 1/3rd abatement on value) on construction service, fixed vide Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

The DGAP also stated that the additional ITC of 3.29 per cent of the taxable turnover should have resulted in commensurate reduction in the base price as well as cum-tax price, in terms of section 171 and this benefit of the additional ITC was required to be passed on to the recipients.

The respondent had denied the allegations regarding profiteering and claimed that the methodolgy used by the DGAP was faulty and had no legal backing in as far as excluding the credit of VAT available to the respondent during the pre-GST era from the calculations of ratios of credit to the turnover was concerned.

There is no doubt that the project undertaken by the applicant pertains to an affordable housing project. In the subject project, the applicant will be constructing dwelling units of less than 60 sq. mtrs. carpet area as well as dwelling units having carpet area greater than 60 sq. mtrs. [Para 5.14.1] It is found that common amenities form part of the overall construction service and are always naturally bundled when offered to the customer. Therefore, such services will qualify as composite supply of works contract service, where the principal supply would be, construction services. Accordingly, the rate applicable to the principal supply will also be applicable to common amenities. The word 'housing project' cannot be confined only to dwelling units, it would also include within its fold, other common amenities, structures, etc. Common amenities form part of the overall construction service and are always naturally bundled when offered to the customer. Therefore, such services will qualify as composite supply of works contract service wherein provision of construction services is the principal supply. Accordingly, the rate applicable to the principal supply will also be applicable to common amenities i.e. in respect of dwelling units having area less than 60 sq. mtrs., the GST rate would be 12 per cent and in cases of dwelling units having area greater than 60 sq. mtrs. the GST rate would be 18 per cent. [Para 5.14.2]

It is held that the applicant's case is covered under the concessional rate of 12 per cent (8 per cent GST after deducting value of land), under Heading 9954 (Construction Services), (v)(da) of above mentioned Notification No. 11/2017, as amended since the project undertaken by them falls under the definition of 'Affordable Housing'. The benefit of reduced rate would be available to them only in the cases of supply effected after 25-1-2018 i.e., the date on which Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate) was issued and the benefit of this reduced rate would be applicable only in case of amenities pertaining to only those flats which are of carpet area upto 60 sq. mtrs. In case of amenities provided to purchasers of flats which have carpet area more than 60 sq. mtrs., the applicant would be required to pay GST at normal applicable rate i.e. at the rate of 18 per cent GST. [Para 5.14]

Subject project consists of both, dwelling units less than and also greater than 60 sq. mtrs. Benefit of concessional rate is only available to 'Affordable Housing' as already discussed above. The definition of 'Affordable Housing' is confined to dwelling units with carpet area of not more than 60 square meters. Thus, concessional rate available to applicant is only in respect of low cost houses along with amenities constructed by the applicant. The common amenities and areas are a part of 'Affordable Housing Project' and therefore the applicant will be entitled to benefit of concessional rate for the same, only when they are a part of low cost houses, i.e. units less than 60 sq. mtrs. The applicant will thus have to discharge GST at the rate of 12 per cent (after deducting value of land) on works contract services provided for the construction of the units and common areas and amenities, which do qualify the criteria of low cost houses. Since concessional rate would be available only for construction services pertaining to dwelling units less than 60 sq. mtrs. Including common areas and amenities on pro rata basis, construction services including common areas and amenities on pro rata basis, performed by the applicant in respect of dwelling units exceeding 60 sq. mtrs. would be liable to full rate of GST, i.e., 18 per cent. [Para 5.14.4]

In the application itself it is stated that MPPGCL has been established by the Government of Madhya Pradesh and the Government of Madhya Pradesh has a 100 per cent shareholding in the company and is also exercising full control over the activities of the said company. Thus, MPPGCL qualifies to be called and termed as a 'Government Entity' for the purpose of GST law, as it fulfils the necessary and sufficient conditions laid down under notification No. 11/2017. [Para 5.4]

Now, the said Government Entity i.e. MPPGCL has been entrusted with the work of power generation in the State of Madhya Pradesh. The essential and sole work entrusted to MPPGCL by the Government of Madhya Pradesh is of electricity (power) generation. MPPGCL has awarded a works contract for construction of 599 residential quarters to the applicant. However, the civil construction of residential quarters is neither the primary work entrusted to MPPGCL nor it has any bearing on the work i.e. power generation by any means. Thus, the benefit of concessional rate of 12 per cent GST should not be available to this particular works contract awarded to the applicant. The intention of the legislature has been to give concessional rate to such work which has been entrusted to a Government entity for public interest in general. Any work having direct involvement in the entrusted work i.e. power generation would merit exemption envisaged under Sr.No.3(vi)(c) of the Notification No.11/2017-CT (Rate) under CGST Act and corresponding notification under MPGST Act 2017, but extrapolating and extending this concessional rate to any or all activities of MPPGCL will not only be unwarranted but also defeat the very purpose of concessional rate. [Para 5.5]

The activity in question definitely did not have any relation to the principal work of power generation entrusted by the State Government to MPPGCL, and, thus, the works contract service of construction of residential quarters would attract GST at the rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) in terms of Notification No.11/2017-CT Rate dated 28-6-2017 and corresponding notification under MPGST Act, 2017. Ltd. arguing that the aforesaid order dated 18-10-2018 is not applicable as the information before the Authority was insufficient and inconclusive to arrive at the ruling. [Para 7.4]

The applicant has argued that the Government of Madhya Pradesh incorporated M.P. Power Generating Co. Ltd. with an object to construct, operate and maintain electricity system as defined in section 2(25) of Electricity Act, 2003 (Power Projects). It has been argued by the applicant that the work of power project includes the entrusting all work related to that project including the work of construction of residential colonies as they are in relation to the power project which is entrusted by the Government. [Para 7.5]

The Authority is not inclined to subscribe to the contentions of the applicant. One of the recommendations made by the GST Council in its 25th meeting held on 18-1-2018 at Delhi was to extend the concessional rate of 12 per cent (8 per cent GST after deducting value of land) to services by way of construction of low cost houses up to a carpet area of 60 sq. m. in a housing project which has been given infrastructure status under Notification No. 13/06/2009, dated 30-3-2009. The said notification of Department of Economic Affairs provides infrastructure status to Affordable Housing. The recommendation of the Council would extend the concessional rate to construction of flats/houses of less than 60 sq. m. in projects other than the projects covered by any scheme of the Central or State Government also. The GST Council has also observed that it may be recalled that all inputs used in and capital goods deployed for construction of flats, houses, etc. attract GST of 18 per cent or 28 per cent. As against this, most of the housing projects in the affordable segment in the country would now attract GST of 8 per cent (after deducting value of land). As a result, the builder or developer will not be required to pay GST on the construction service of flats etc. in cash but would have enough ITC (input tax credits) in his books to pay the output GST, in which case, he should not recover any GST payable on the flats from the buyers. He can recover GST from the buyers of flats only if he recalibrates the cost of flat after factoring in the full ITC available in the GST regime and reduces the ex-GST price of flats. The GST Council has also mentioned that the builders/developers are expected to follow the principles laid down under section 171 of the GST Act (Anti-Profiteering Rules) scrupulously.

Ruling

The parking services provided by the contractor (applicant) appointed by the Market Committee are not exempt under Notification No. 12/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as the Market Committee is not a Government Authority. Sl. No. 3(vi)(a) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is the relevant entry which prescribes GST rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST+6 per cent SGST) in respect of services provided to the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority, a Government Authority or a Government Entity by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession. Thus to attract rate of tax at 12 per cent under Sl. No. 3(vi)(a), the specified service should primarily be provided to the Central Government/State Government/Union Territory/local authority/Government Authority/Government Entity and must be used for other than commercial, industrial, or any other business or professional activity.

Now it is required to examine the question whether the contractee in the instant case, i.e., TSSPDCL falls under the specified categories of recipient viz. Central Government/State Government/Union Territory/local authority/Governmental Authority/Government Entity on not. The phrase 'Government Entity' is defined under the Explanation appended to Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. The same reads as:

'Government Entity' means an authority or a board or any other body including a society, trust, corporation.

(i)

Set up by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature; or

(ii)

Established by any Government,

with 90 per cent or more participation by way of equity or control, to carry out a function entrusted by the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory or a local authority.

It is apparent from the schedule concerning 'shareholding of promoter' of the annual accounts of TSSPDCL that 100 per cent shares of the company were held by the Governor of Telangana. This clear indicates that the Government of Telangana have 100 per cent control over TSSPDCL. Thus TSSPDCL is evidently covered under the definition of 'Government Entity'.

The next issue to be decided in this regard is whether the impugned services supplied by the applicant are for the works which are used for other than commerce, industry, or any other business or profession. As per the details furnished by the applicant, the works undertaken are for execution/implementation of various projects for (i) Capacitor Bank Works in Nalgonda etc., (ii) HVDS-High Voltage Distribution Systems in Suryapet used for agricultural feeders. The applicant further stated that the Government of Telangana is reimbursing the money to TSSPDCL on behalf of the customers for agricultural services rendered. Thus TSSPDCL is not rendering any non-commercial services inasmuch as it is getting reimbursed for its activity on behalf of its customers. Therefore, this activity cannot be termed as other than commercial/business purposes.

The impugned works undertaken are for business/commercial purposes. Therefore, the benefit of concessional rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) is not applicable to the services supplied by the applicant. Further the services supplied by the applicant are subjected to 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) in terms of Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

Ruling

The applicant is not entitled for the benefit of concessional rate of GST at 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) in respect of the works quoted in application in terms of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 2-6-2017 or any other concessional rate.

Whether a particular person is a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity is to be decided in terms of the definition adduced under Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 by applying the facts of each case.

The impugned works are used for commercial/business activities in view of the facts and circumstances and accordingly the same are taxable under GST Act.

The applicable rate of tax is 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) for the services referred to by the applicant. [Para 8]

On a plain reading of the entries at Item (i) and (ia) of Sl. [Para 9]

From the definition of the term 'apartment', 'residential apartment', 'real estate project', and 'promoter' as defined in section 2 of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 it is clear that the residential villas being constructed by the applicant fall within the definition of residential apartment and the projects undertaken by the applicant including the redevelopment projects fall within the definition of real estate project and the applicant fall within the definition of 'promoter'. The services of construction of villas provided by the applicant squarely fall within the description of services specified in Item (i) and (ia) of Sl. No. 3 of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 3/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019. Accordingly the tax rates as prescribed in the said entries shall be applicable to the said services supplied by the applicant. The applicant is liable to pay GST at the rate of 1.5 per cent [0.75 per cent CGST + 0.75 per cent SGST] in respect of the services of construction of affordable residential apartments as per entry at Item (i) and at the rate of 7.5 per cent [3.75 per cent CGST + 3.75 per cent SGST] in respect of the services of construction of residential apartments other than affordable residential apartments as per entry at Item No. (ia) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 subject to the conditions prescribed under the respective entries.

The next question raised by the applicant is regarding the taxable value of the services of construction of residential villas rendered by it. Both the entries at Item (i) and (ia) of Sl. No. 3 of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 specify that the provisions of Paragraph 2 of the said notification shall apply for valuation of the service.

In terms of Para 2 of the above Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 the taxable value in respect of the service specified at Item (i) and (ia) of Sl. No. 3 of the said Notification is the total amount charged for the supply less the value of land or undivided share of land and the value of land or undivided share of land shall be deemed to be one-third of the total amount charged for the supply. The CBIC in FAQ's on Real Estate Sector issued under F. No. 354/32/2019 - TRU dated 7-5-2019 has clarified as follows:

Question No. 36: Can a developer take deduction of actual value of land involved in sale of unit instead of taking deduction of deemed value of land as per Paragraph 2 to Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017?

Ans: No. Valuation mechanism prescribed in paragraph 2 of the notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 clearly prescribes one-third abatement towards value of land.

Therefore, the value of land or undivided share of land is deemed to be one-third of the total amount charged for the supply irrespective of the actual value of land and accordingly the applicant is eligible to avail deduction of one-third of the total amount charged for the supply in arriving at the taxable value of the supply. [Para 11]

Andhra Pradesh State Financial Corporation (APSFC) is a term lending institution established in 1956 for promoting small and medium scale industries in Andhra Pradesh under the provisions of the State Financial Corporation Act, 1951. The functions of the corporation are to launch entrepreneur friendly schemes to provide term loans, working capital term loans, special and seed capital assistance, etc.

The APSFC is established by the Government and the Government of Andhra Pradesh is having more than 90 per cent of control over it. Thus it is covered under the definition of 'Government Entity'. Therefore, the APSFC is a 'Government Entity' for the purpose of GST matters.

The applicant agreed for construction of office building to APSFC, which includes procurement and supply of goods and services for agreed consideration. The activity of construction includes both supply of goods and also services.

Section 2(119) defines 'works contract' as a contract for building, construction, fabrication, completion, erection, installation, fitting out, improvement, modification, repair, maintenance, renovation, alternation or commissioning of any immovable property wherein transfer of property in goods (whether as goods or in some other form) is involved in the execution of such contract.

The composite supply of works contract under section 2(119) is treated as supply of service in terms of Serial No. 6(a) of Schedule II of the CGST Act.

The Government of India vide Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 notified the rate of GST applicable on supply of services. Under this Notification for Heading No. 9954, the applicable rate of GST is 9 per cent.

Vide Notification No. 24/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017, Government of India by inserting entry (vi) notified concessional GST rate of 6 per cent for the construction services provided to Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority or a Governmental Authority by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of —

(a)

a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession;

(b)

a structure meant predominantly for use as (i) an educational, (ii) a clinical, or (iii) an art or cultural establishment; or

(c)

a residential complex predominantly meant for self-use or the use of their employees or other persons specified in paragraph 3 of the Schedule III of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.

The applicant is engaged in construction work of office building for APSFC, which is meant for governance of corporation activities. The applicant is of the view that the use of the said construction (building) is not for any business or so.

As seen from the Annual Reports for the years 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2017-18 as made available by APSFC in its website, it is engaged in providing financial services to industries and entrepreneurs. The income it is getting is from interest on loans and advances and also service charges, upfront fee/commitment fee, sale of application forms, profit on sale of assets, commission on insurance, rent received, etc. Therefore, the activities of APSFC are business activities and not otherwise. The applicant informed that the said building is for use as office by APSFC. Therefore, it appears that the said construction is for office use for conducting business activities of APSFC. Moreover the applicant did not provide any information or documentary proof evidencing that the construction/building is for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession to be eligible for concessional rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) available under Notification No. 24/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017.

In the instant case, the contract entered by the applicant is classifiable under Heading No. 9954 under construction services and it falls under entry (ii) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, i.e., composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and the applicable rate of tax is 18 per cent (9 per cent under Central Tax and 9 per cent under State Tax).

Ruling

The activity of the applicant under the agreement with APSFC is a composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.

GVSCCL is a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) created by the Government of Andhra Pradesh. GVSCCL is a limited company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013 in which the Andhra Pradesh State Government and the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation are the promoters having 50:50 equity shareholding, which substantiates more than 90 per cent of participation of the Government. With reference to the 'control' wielded by the shareholders, all the directors of the board are public authorities. Initially the board was constituted with the Principal Secretary for Municipal Administration and Urban Development, Govt. of A.P. (under promoter category) as chairman. The District Collector and Commissioner, GVMC (under Promoter Category) and other 11 members were nominated by the Authorities in the State Government, ULB and Central Government as per the said G.O. The SPV is owned by the Government of A.P. and GVMC on 50:50 ratio and is governed by a Board of Directors answerable to the Government of A.P., Government of India and GVMC. The Government of A.P. and GVMC are the shareholders in the GVSCCL.

Accordingly, the GVSCCL rightly fits into the definition of the 'Government Entity' as per Sl. No. 4(x) of Notification No. 31/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017. The functions carried out by the said GVSCCL are the functions which were entrusted by the Central Government, State Government and Local Authority i.e. of Municipal Administration.

Furthermore, the service provided by the applicant is composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2, provided to a Government Entity by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession. The same is classifiable under the Heading No. 9954 Entry at Sl. No. 3(vi)(a) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended from time to time and liable to tax at the rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST).

The benefits of tax rate reduction and ITC have been given by the State and the Central Govt. from their own tax revenue to provide accommodation to the vulnerable sections of society under the Affordable Housing Schemes. The method of interpretation of this provision has been given in the text of section 171. The above provision clearly links profiteering with each supply of goods or services or both and hence, profiteering has to be computed at the level of both. Therefore, the respondent is under legal obligation to pass on the benefit of ITC to his buyers and he cannot be allowed to appropriate the same. [Para 53]

Based on the above facts it is clear that the ITC as a percentage of the turnover that was available to the respondent during the pre-GST period from April, 2016 to June, 2017 was 4.76 per cent and during the post-GST period from July, 2017 to December, 2018, it was 7.27 per cent as hence it is established that the Respondent has benefited from the benefit of additional ITC to the extent of 2.51 per cent [7.27 per cent (-) 4.76 per cent] of the turnover. Since, the above computations have been made on the basis of the VAT, Service Tax and GST Returns filed by the respondent as well as the information supplied by him therefore, the same can be taken to be correct and relied upon. [Para 54]

It is also clear from the record that the Central Government, on the recommendation of the GST Council, had levied 18 per cent GST with effective rate of 12 per cent in view of 1/3rd abatement on value on the construction service, vide Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-06-2017, which was reduced in the case of affordable housing from 12 per cent to 8 per cent, vide Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018. Accordingly, the DGAP has computed the profiteered amount by comparing the applicable tax rate and ITC available in the pre-GST period when only VAT at the rate of 4.50 per cent was payable with (1) the post-GST period from 1-7-2017 to 24-1-2018, when the effective GST rate was 12 per cent and (2) with the GST period from 25-1-2018 to 31-12-2018, when the effective GST rate was 8 per cent. Accordingly, the DGAP has calculated the profiteered amount or the benefit to be passed on for the period from 1-7-2017 to 24-1-2018, as Rs. 1,16,75,749/- for the residential flats and commercial shops, which includes 12 per cent GST on the base profiteered amount of Rs. 1,04,24,775/-. He has also computed the amount of benefit of ITC or the profiteered amount that needs to be passed on by the Respondent to his recipients during the period from 25-1-2018 to 31-12-2018, as Rs. 2,42,15,122/- which includes 12 per cent GST on commercial shops and 8 per cent GST on residential flats, on the base profiteered amount of Rs. 2,23,88,036/-. Therefore, the total benefit of ITC which is required to be passed on during the period from 1-7-2017 to 31-12-2018, comes to Rs. 3,58,90,871/- which includes GST at the rate of 12 per cent or 8 per cent on the base profiteered amount of Rs. 3,28,12,811/-. [Para 55]

In view of the above facts this Authority under Rule 133 (3) (a) of the CGST Rules, 2017, orders that the respondent shall reduce the prices to be realized from the buyers of the flats commensurate with the benefit of ITC received by him as has been mentioned in detail in the preceding paras of this Order. [Para 56]

One of the recommendations made by the GST Council in its 25th meeting held on 18th January, 2018 at Delhi was to extend the concessional rate of 12% (8% GST after deducting value of land) to services by way of construction of low cost houses up to a carpet area of 60 sqm in a housing project which has been given infrastructure status under Notification No. 13/06/2009. The said Notification of Department of Economic Affairs provides infrastructure status to Affordable Housing. The recommendation of the Council would extend the concessional rate to construction of flats/houses of less than 60 sqm. in projects other than the projects covered by any scheme of the Central or State Government also. The GST Council has also observed that "It may be recalled that all inputs used in and capital goods deployed for construction of flats, houses, etc. attract GST of 18% or 28%. As against this, most of the housing projects in the affordable segment in the country would now attract GST of 8% (after deducting value of land). As a result, the builder or developer will not be required to pay GST on the construction service of flats etc. in cash but would have enough ITC (input tax credits) in his books to pay the output GST, in which case, he should not recover any GST payable on the flats from the buyers. He can recover GST from the buyers of flats only if he recalibrates the cost of the flat after factoring in the full ITC available in the GST regime and reduces the ex-GST price of flats." The GST Council has also mentioned that the builders/developers are expected to follow the principles laid down under Section 171 of the GST Act (Anti-Profiteering Rules) scrupulously.

In response to a request for clarification to enable availing 8% GST on Affordable Housing made by the builders association namely, CREDAI, vide their letter No. CREDAI/MoF/2018/14, dated 19th March, 2018, the Government, vide F.No. 354/52/2018-TRU, G.O.I, M.O.F., Deptt. of Revenue (TRU), dated 7th May, 2018 has clarified that "Low cost houses up to a carpet area of 60 square metres per house in an affordable housing project, which has been given infrastructure status under Notification F. No. 13/6/2009-INF, dated the 30th March, 2017 of MOF (DEA), attract concessional GST of 8% (the value of the undivided share of land is included in the price of the house). Whether the housing project qualifies as affordable housing project or not, shall be determined by the builder/developer as per the definition of affordable housing given in the abovementioned notification (i.e., affordable housing has been defined as a housing project using at least 50% of FAR/FSI for dwelling units with carpet area of not more than 60 SQM). No certificate from any authority is required."

We find that applicant has not been given the entire contract for construction of complete houses. Probably the carpentry work like making of doors, etc., electrical work, etc. does not seem to have been given to them. However we also find that the job allotted to them are pertaining to affordable housing since the each and every one of the apartments are less than 60 sq. mtrs. We find that entry (v)(da) of Notification 01/2018, mentioned above, no-where restricts the benefit to a 'Developer' only. The Notification entry is qua the supply of service and not qua the person and therefore once a project qualifies as an AHP, the benefit of concessional rate of tax would be available in respect of works contract services pertaining to Low Cost Houses, irrespective of it being supplied by the Developer or the Contractor. Hence, in view of the above discussions and facts on record, we find that that the applicant's case is covered under the tax rate of 12%, under Heading 9954 (Construction Services), (v)(da) of above mentioned Notification No. 11/2017, as amended since the project undertaken by them falls under the definition of "Affordable Housing" as also claimed by them in their application. The benefit of reduced rate would be available to them only in the cases of supply effected after 25.01.2018 i.e. the date on which Notification 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate) was issued and the benefit of this reduced rate would be applicable in case of only those flats which are of carpet area upto 60 sq. mtrs., in this scheme, which is covered in the category of affordable housing.

5.2 The applicant contended that the Airport Authority of India is a statutory body (created through the Airports Authority of India Act, 1994) working under the jurisdiction of Directorate General of Civil Aviation, Ministry of Civil Aviation, Government of India is responsible for creating, upgrading, maintaining and managing civil aviation infrastructure in India. It provides Communication Navigation Surveillance/Air Traffic Management (CNS/ATM) services over Indian airspace and adjoining oceanic areas. AAI is currently managing a total of 137[1] Airports, including 23[1] International Airports, 10 Customs Airports, 81 Domestic Airports and 23 Civil enclaves at Defense Airfields. AAI also has ground installations at all airports and 25 other locations to ensure safety of aircraft operations.

5.3 In the instant case, the applicant is supplying construction services to Airport Authority of India. Airport Authority of India is a statutory body established vide Airport Authority of India Act, 1994. Section 12 of the Act provides for functions of the authority. It is, inter alia, provided that it shall be the duty of the Authority to manage airports and civil enclaves and aeronautical communication stations and to provide air traffic service and air transport service at all airports and civil enclaves. In Ramana Dayaram Shetty v. International Airport Authority AIR 1979 SC 1628, the Supreme Court held that International Airport Authority constituted under the International Airport Authority Act, 1971 was an authority and thus, 'state' within the meaning of Article 12 of the Constitution. Thus, AAI satisfies the first leg of the above definition.

5.4 The applicant submitted that the term "governmental authority" has been defined under Notification No. 31/2017-CT (R) dated 13-10-2017. It defines governmental authority to mean an authority or a board or any other body which has been (i) set up by an Act of Parliament or a State Legislature; or (ii) established by any Government, with 90 per cent or more participation by way of equity or control, to carry out any function entrusted to a Municipality under article 243W of the Constitution or to a Panchayat under Article 243G of the Constitution. A similar definition existed under Notification No. 25/2012-ST dated 20-6-2012 under the erstwhile service tax law regime.

Illustration:

Suppose an instalment is due at the time of completion of a particular floor and that floor is completed on 27th August, 2017. In present service tax regime, the developer can issue its invoice within 30 days i.e. up to 26th September, 2017. However, in GST regime, the invoice have to be issued before or at time of completion of service i.e. 27th August, 2017.

Effective Rate of Tax As per the draft list of rates released by the GST council after its meeting on 18.05.2017, rate of GST applicable on construction sector is 12%, where the value of land is included in the purchase consideration. There is no further abatement/composition on this rate. Further, person cannot claim refund of Input Tax Credit (ITC) accumulated on account of higher tax rates on inputs/input services than on the rate of output. In other words, in case of accumulation of ITC because of the fact that tax rates on some inputs or input services will be 18% or even 28%, its refund will not be allowed to the assessee.

Further, if the value of land is not included, then the rate of tax applicable would be 18% (under service of Works Contract).

In addition, all special services provided by builders like preferential location charges (PLC), power backup charges (PBC), club service, administrative charges, cheque return, booking transfer charges etc. would be chargeable at the rate of 18%.

However, one issue for consideration is the treatment of car parking charges that are recovered separately from a flat buyer. Some people might argue that buying flat is a pre-requisite for buying such car parking space and hence supply of flat and car parking space are naturally bundled in course of business and will thus fall under the category of composite supply and accordingly rate of 12% will be applicable on the car parking charges also. It would a close call on the part of developers and would definitely invite litigation from the GST department. Thus, to be safer side the builder might charge 18% rate on car parking charges.

The government also released a classification for services as per Service Accounting Code (SAC) under GST regime. As per the said scheme, a separate Section (Section 5: Construction Services) has been provided for the Construction service which is further sub-divided into headings and groups. Developers need to ascertain their category and SAC for various purposes under GST regime.

Further, rate chart for major significant inputs used in the construction industry and their rates in present as well as GST regime is given below:
